narrative:
Your loan application was denied because the model estimated a 27% chance that you would be a bad credit risk—roughly one in four applicants with a similar profile. That is below a simple coin flip, but it is above the bank’s conservative cutoff for this loan, so the application did not proceed.

The strongest influence was the very short requested term: six months, compared with an approved average of about 19 months. This worked in your favour, lowering the assessed risk. Your credit history was the second-most important factor and also moved the assessment toward good credit. The third and most concerning factor was your checking-account status: a balance below zero is much less common among approved applicants—about 13% versus 59% with no negative/overdrawn pattern—and this pushed the prediction toward bad credit. That warning signal, together with other less favourable details in your profile, kept the overall risk above the bank’s threshold.

To improve a future application, bring your checking account into a non-negative position and resolve any critical credit issues before reapplying. Ask the lender what specific risk cutoff or documentation would make a new application competitive, and consider reapplying only after those signals have improved.
